title: How Much Space Makes a Figure?
selectionMethod: Internal 1-5 judgments in order: originality, visual necessity, interaction meaning, feasibility. Reasons, not totals, determine the choice. Scores are planning notes, never displayed as evidence or outcomes.

hypotheses.idea: Move one fixed square from frame contact to the center beside an identical centered reference
hypotheses.reason: Selected: shape, area, perimeter, orientation and color stay fixed while a simultaneous reference makes the changing margin directly inspectable.

hypotheses.idea: Move a disk from frame contact to the center beside a fixed disk
hypotheses.reason: The control is equally clear, but Day024 should answer Day023 with the same square geometry rather than introducing curvature as a new visual cue.

hypotheses.idea: Increase padding around a fixed word until it appears like a label
hypotheses.reason: Editorially relevant, but language, legibility and semantic enclosure would compete with the narrower figure-ground question.

hypotheses.idea: Slide a square across all four frame edges on a two-dimensional pad
hypotheses.reason: It would reveal more positions but would make direct keyboard parity and a legible one-variable sequence less precise than a linear margin control.

hypotheses.idea: Compare equal squares at the corner, edge midpoint and center
hypotheses.reason: Three simultaneous states are printable, but a continuous visitor-controlled margin better exposes where contact ends without pretending to locate a threshold.

hypotheses.idea: Add a second frame around the same square while preserving its position
hypotheses.reason: Nested framing could be visually rich, but frame weight and enclosure count would change while the unresolved contact question remained indirect.

hypotheses.idea: Move an equal square behind and in front of a frame stroke
hypotheses.reason: Layer order would become the dominant cue and would shift the inquiry toward occlusion rather than spacing from a boundary.

hypotheses.idea: Let visitors draw the smallest gap that feels separated
hypotheses.reason: A threshold response would be interesting, but recording it would imply measurement and introduce privacy, protocol and participant requirements not met today.

hypotheses.idea: Animate the square away from the frame and stop at random margins
hypotheses.reason: Motion history and timing would become extra variables, and reduced-motion visitors would receive a structurally different experiment.

hypotheses.idea: Compare the same square on calibrated and uncalibrated color pairs
hypotheses.reason: Display calibration cannot be verified remotely and would distract from the geometric control while overstating color precision.

variable: The adjustable square's horizontal margin from its selected frame edge, from 0% contact to the mathematically centered 33% position.
comparison: A fixed centered reference and an adjustable condition show squares that are both 34% of field width and height, with identical color, area, perimeter and orientation.
constants: Equal square field dimensions in the same viewport
Same 34% by 34% square geometry in both fields
Same two opaque sRGB color values and full opacity
Same vertical center, frame stroke and square orientation
No stored response, score, external media or participant-data collection
challenge: If judgments vary, reverse with color or side, or are better explained by centrality, position, frame terminology or display conditions, do not attribute a general figure-ground effect to margin or edge contact. The implementation cannot separate contact from horizontal position.
researchLedForm: Two equal fields lead the page. The reference square remains centered while the matching square travels on one horizontal axis from touching the frame to occupying the same centered position. A native range, three semantic presets, side mirror, color swap and reset expose the construction without naming a correct answer.
mediaDecision: Responsive HTML and CSS keep two exact square geometries synchronized and let keyboard, pointer and touch users inspect continuous margin states. A still freezes the variable; video adds timing; generated imagery cannot guarantee exact responsive insets or flat color. No external image, video, audio or generated asset is used.

revisits.question: Counterbalance side, color, order and starting margin; ask contact, figure, dominance and confidence separately without presenting the center as an answer.

Compare edge contact with position held closer to constant through masking or moving frames, and inspect whether shipping design tools expose relational spacing without reducing perception to a score.
